Render error when combining multiple input parameters in docstring **Describe the bug & Reproduce** My team is writing a function in Python, which contains 3 inputs that are similar, so we want to put them in the same line in the docstring. As described in 4. Parameters in [numpydoc docstring guide](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html#sections), this is possible if you write something like this: ``` x1, x2 : array_like Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` However, this produces: Even worse, when added "optional", the rendered HTML stays the same as the screenshot above, so there is no way to tell whether it is optional: ``` x1, x2 : array_like, optional Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` **Expected behavior** Something like - x1, x2 (_array_like, optional_) - Input arrays, description of x1, x2. **Environment info** - OS: macOS 10.15.5 (19F101) - Python version: 3.7.7 - Sphinx version: 3.0.3. - Extra tools: browser: Firefox 79.0a1 or Safari 13.1.1 - Sphinx extensions: ``` extensions = [ "sphinx.ext.autodoc", "sphinx.ext.todo", "sphinx.ext.coverage", "sphinx.ext.extlinks", "sphinx.ext.intersphinx", "sphinx.ext.mathjax", "sphinx.ext.viewcode", "sphinx.ext.napoleon", "nbsphinx", "sphinx.ext.mathjax", "sphinxcontrib.bibtex", "sphinx.ext.doctest", ] ``` # Plan ## Problem When a numpydoc "Parameters" entry lists several names on one line using the numpydoc-supported syntax: ``` x1, x2 : array_like, optional Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` the napoleon Numpy parser emits a single malformed docutils type field for the whole combined name: ``` :param x1, x2: Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. :type x1, x2: :class:`array_like`, *optional* ``` `:type:` expects a single parameter name as its argument. `x1, x2` is not a valid target, so the type (and the `optional` marker inside it) is not rendered — exactly the bug in the screenshot. The `:param x1, x2:` line is fine because docutils treats the param field body as text. The non-default path (`napoleon_use_param=False`, i.e. the `:Parameters:` field-list style) already renders correctly, as reproduced locally: ``` :Parameters: **x1, x2** (:class:`array_like`, *optional*) -- Input arrays, description of x1, x2. ``` So the defect is confined to the default `napoleon_use_param=True` code path. ## Root cause In `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py`, `NumpyDocstring._format_docutils_params` (line ~389) writes the type field with the raw combined name: ```python if _type: lines.append(':%s %s: %s' % (type_role, _name, _type)) ``` `_name` here is `"x1, x2"` (the Numpy `_consume_field` splits the name only on the colon, not on commas). The Google-style `GoogleDocstring._consume_field` has the same combined-name behavior, and `_format_docutils_params` is shared by both `NumpyDocstring` and `GoogleDocstring` (used from `_parse_keyword_arguments_section` and `_parse_parameters_section`), so both dialects are affected. ## Proposed change Change `_format_docutils_params` so that, when a parameter name contains multiple comma-separated names, it emits one `:type:` line per individual name instead of one combined line. Keep the single `:param ...:` line as-is (docutils renders its argument text fine, and the joined names read naturally). Conceptual shape of the fix (exact placement to be finalized during implementation): ```python if _type: for _name in _name.split(','): lines.append(':%s %s: %s' % (type_role, _name.strip(), _type)) ``` Verified locally that this produces valid output for the reported input: ``` :param x1, x2: Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. :type x1: :class:`array_like`, *optional* :type x2: :class:`array_like`, *optional* ``` This makes the type and the `optional` qualifier render for each named parameter, resolving the second half of the report (the `optional` marker disappearing). Note the pre-existing `_escape_args_and_kwargs` override on `NumpyDocstring` already understands comma-separated names (it splits on `", "` to escape `*args, **kwargs`), so the codebase already treats "one field, several names" as a supported case; the fix keeps that convention. ## Why not split names upstream Splitting the name inside `_consume_field` into separate fields would change the `:param:` output too (producing two `:param x1:` / `:param x2:` lines and duplicating the description), which is not what numpydoc documents and not what the reporter wants. The docutils `:param x1, x2:` text form already renders acceptably, so restricting the change to the `:type:` emission is the minimal, targeted fix. ## Retype / other sections Only `_format_docutils_params` needs changing. The `:rtype:` handling in `_parse_returns_section`/`_consume_returns_section` deals with a single return, and the `napoleon_use_param=False` field-list path (`_format_fields` → `_format_field`) already handles combined names correctly (the `**x1, x2** (type)` form), so no change is needed there. ## Tests `tests/test_ext_napoleon_docstring.py` already has the surrounding fixtures (e.g. `test_parameters_with_class_reference` around line 1320, and the `test_escape_args_and_kwargs` parametrization around line 2248 that pins the comma-splitting convention). Add a test covering a multi-name parameter in the default (`use_param=True`) mode, asserting the generated lines contain one `:type:` per name, e.g. for `x1, x2 : array_like, optional` expect: ``` :param x1, x2: Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. :type x1: :class:`array_like`, *optional* :type x2: :class:`array_like`, *optional* ``` Add a parallel case exercising the same input under `napoleon_use_param=False` only if the existing suite does not already lock that behavior, to guard the unchanged path. ## Documentation / changelog Add a bullet under "Bugs fixed" in `CHANGES` (Release 3.2.0 in development section, near line 60) describing that napoleon now renders the type of multi-name parameters listed in one field.
